dependencyRules.reason: An adapter serves ports and must not reach back into a delivery surface.
Use cases drive outbound ports; a concrete adapter is injected at composition, never imported.
A use case cannot depend on the surface that invoked it.
A delivery surface reaches the domain only through the application layer, so product logic cannot migrate into a screen.
The centre cannot reach a technology-specific implementation.
The centre cannot know about the use cases that orchestrate it.
The centre cannot know it is being rendered.
An adapter may reference the domain types it moves.
An adapter exists to implement a port.
Use cases are declared by and drive their ports.
A surface may reference inbound port contracts.
A port may reference the domain types it carries.
An adapter implementing no declared port has no reason to exist and is a violation.

isolation.reason: The centre must be usable unchanged from a browser, a server, a mobile shell and a protocol server. One framework or host import in those layers ends that property silently.

cyclePolicy.scope: Every module beneath packages/ and apps/ in the ANQR product repository.

scopeRules.runtime: Components in the domain, ports and application layers may depend at runtime only on the language standard library.
scopeRules.development: Type checking, testing, boundary analysis and bundling are development-only and may never become runtime imports of those layers.

generated.location: Any path whose name declares it generated, and localised content resources produced by the translation pipeline.
generated.consumerRule: Generated code may be imported by the delivery and adapter layers only. No domain, port or application module may depend on it, so regeneration can never change product meaning.

testBoundaries.mayImport: A built delivery surface as a user reaches it.
testBoundaries.mayNotImport: Product internals reached other than through the surface.

testBoundaries.mayImport: Only a component's declared public entry point.
testBoundaries.mayNotImport: Any internal module of the component under test.

testBoundaries.mayImport: Real adapters and the application layer.
The module under test and its own layer.
testBoundaries.mayNotImport: Any adapter, any delivery surface, and any network, filesystem or clock.

moduleBoundaries.name: assurance-and-test-tooling
scope: packages/architecture/ and packages/artefact/tests/ in the ANQR product repository.
forbids: No module of a declared architectural component may import from packages/architecture/ or from any test location. Assurance code observes the architecture and must never become something the architecture depends on.
moduleBoundaries.reason: Enforcement machinery and tests are owned code that belongs to no layer of the product. Naming them as an excluded scope means every source is attributable: assigned to a component, or covered by a declared exclusion. Without it the honest count of unaccounted sources cannot be asserted to be zero, and an unaccounted source is a hiding place.

moduleBoundaries.name: released-capability-convention
scope: src/capabilities/ and tests/conformance/ in the ANQR product repository.
forbids: No module of a declared architectural component may import from src/capabilities/ or tests/conformance/. Those paths are the released one-module-per-capability convention, which predates this architecture and is deliberately outside the hexagonal component model; letting a component depend on them would make the released convention load-bearing for the new topology.
moduleBoundaries.reason: Without this rule the released capability tree is a hiding place: 78 source files belong to no declared component, so a dependency-direction check that only compares assigned components would never see a violation placed among them. Naming the boundary makes the exclusion explicit and checkable instead of silent.
